[[File:Erythrina senegalensis MHNT.BOT.2010.10.6.jpg|thumb|''Erythrina senegalensis'' [[MHNT]]]]

'''''Erythrina senegalensis''''', the '''Senegal coraltree''',<ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN | id = 15765 | accessdate = 18 March 2020}}</ref> is a plant in the pea family [[Fabaceae]], native to West Africa.

==Description==
''Erythrina senegalensis'' grows as a tree up to {{convert|7|m|0}} tall, rarely to {{convert|15|m|-1|abbr=on}}. The bark is fissured. The leaves are composed of three leaflets which measure up to {{convert|15|cm|0|abbr=on}} long, on a thorny stalk. [[Glossary of botanical terms#inflorescence|Inflorescences]] have many flowers with bright red petals. The seeds are poisonous.<ref name=POWO/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Erythrina senegalensis'' is native to West Africa, across the region from Mauritania to Chad and Cameroon. Its habitat is in wooded [[grassland]] or savanna.<ref name=POWO/>

==Uses==
''Erythrina senegalensis'' is locally used in traditional medicine. The wood is locally used to make knife handles and the seeds to make necklaces. The species is cultivated as an ornamental and also used in hedges.<ref name=POWO/>
